items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:9:1
items.html:
There is no difference at all from world to world: It has already been clarified above that in the four phases of direct light there is no difference at all from world to world or from Partzuf to Partzuf, from the Rosh of the Kav to the end of Assiya. For there is no degree at all that does not have within it the four phases of direct light, which are: Hochma, Bina, Tifferet and Malchut. And the whole difference between the degrees is only in the measure of stature of the reflected light (Ohr Pnimi, Part 3, Chapter 3, Item 5), and the measure of stature depends on the coarseness of the screen that is in the Malchut of the degree: for the screen of phase four raises reflected light and clothes it up to the stature of Keter. And that of phase three raises reflected light only up to the stature of Hochma, and it lacks the stature of Keter, and the Keter of direct light is forced to clothe within the interiority of Hochma and is not discernible there. And the screen of phase two raises reflected light only up to the stature of Bina, and it also lacks the stature of Hochma, wherefore the Keter and Hochma of direct light clothe here within the interiority of Bina. And the screen of phase one raises reflected light only up to the stature of Tifferet, called ZA, and it also lacks the stature of Bina, wherefore the three first Sefirot KHB clothe within it within the interiority of Tifferet, and are not discernible on account of this. (And see well in the Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 72, Sub Header, "And so that") — see there the whole continuation, to understand the above matters in their reasons and grounds.
And by this you will understand that the five worlds called Adam Kadmon, Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, Assiya, which include the whole of existence from the restriction downward, are also reckoned as ten Sefirot that include the whole of existence, and they are discerned according to the values of the measure of stature that is in the five phases of the screen. For phase four, upon which was the first restriction and the first coupling of striking, behold these first ten Sefirot are the ones called the ten Sefirot, or the four phases, of Adam Kadmon, and their measure of stature is up to the stature of Keter of direct light, as above, and therefore Adam Kadmon is called the world of Keter.
And behold, after the four phases of AK were completed, the screen of phase four was refined to phase three, and the light of Ein Sof, which does not cease, again expands in the four phases of direct light upon this screen of phase three, in a coupling of striking, and here their measure of stature is only up to Hochma, as above, and they are called the ten Sefirot, or the four phases, of the world of Atzilut. And after the world of Atzilut was completed, the screen was again refined to phase two, and ten Sefirot emerged at the stature of Bina, which are called the world of Beria. And after that it was refined to phase one, and ten Sefirot emerged at the stature of Tifferet, called the ten Sefirot, or the four phases, of the world of Yetzira. And after that, when it was refined completely, and no coarseness at all remained in the screen except only a phase of root of coarseness, then there is no striking in it at all, and it has only ten Sefirot at the stature of Malchut alone, which are called the ten Sefirot, or the four phases, of the world of Assiya. And the reason and cause for this refinement is clarified (in the Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 72, mentioned above).
And behold, the ten Sefirot that include the whole of existence have now been well clarified: that the world of AK is the general Keter, and the world of Atzilut is the general Hochma, and the world of Beria is the general Bina, and the world of Yetzira is the general ZA, which is discerned as six Sefirot, HGT NHY, as above, and the world of Assiya is the general Malchut. Indeed, within each and every one of these five worlds there are also particular ten Sefirot, as will be written below in the discourse following this one. And although in every world there are stature-levels one below the other, even in the world of Adam Kadmon — but just as with the particular stature-levels of the ten Sefirot, we reckon the measure of the light of the stature according to the highest Sefira within it, so that if the highest Sefira is Keter, all the Sefirot have the light of Keter, and if the highest Sefira is Hochma, all the Sefirot have Hochma — likewise we reckon the measure of the light of each world according to the first Partzuf within it. So AK is at the stature of Keter, and Atzilut at the stature of Hochma, and Beria at the stature of Bina, and so on.

items.html:
Five discernments of Keter: To explain these matters well requires great length, and it will be clarified here in the Inner Observation; but I will explain here to some measure that will suffice, at least, to order the matters so that we not become confused by the many similar-sounding names, namely the generalities and the particulars and the particulars of particulars, brought in the discourse before us. First let us consider the "Sefira of Keter." For we find here in the words of the Rav five discernments of Keter, each of which he designates by a special name: one, is the Keter of the four phases of direct light. Two, the Keter that includes the four phases in potential. Three, the Keter that includes the four phases in actuality. Four, the Keter that includes a whole world called AK. Five, the Keter of each particular degree in all the worlds, which draw from the world of AK. And know, that although all the aforesaid discernments of Keter are always brought in this wisdom simply under the name Keter without any explanation, nevertheless they are immeasurably distant from one another, and it is impossible to distinguish between them except according to the matter under discussion, wherefore one must first know precisely, at the source, the particular distinction of each one.
Now the Keter of direct light is brought above (Part 3, Chapter 1, Item 1) in the words of the Rav, in the name of the expansion of Ein Sof, blessed be He, in the secret of vessels, and in the secret of the coupling of striking; thus Ein Sof, blessed be He, is the root for the four phases of direct light, called the Keter of direct light, and know that this is the secret of Ein Sof, blessed be He, before the restriction. For there is no renewal of light in the worlds that is not drawn from the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, before the restriction. And you already know that these four phases of direct light apply equally without any difference from the Rosh of the Kav to the end of Assiya, and so too the secret of their Keter.
Indeed, the Keter called Atik, which includes the four phases in potential, as above in the words of the Rav (Part 3, Chapter 6, Item 4), and likewise the Keter called AA, which includes the roots of the four phases in actuality, meaning that it is the complete root for the emanated beings, as above in the words of the Rav (Part 3, Chapter 6, Item 6), are matters entirely distinct in themselves from the discernment of the Keter of direct light mentioned above, for they are discerned as the head of the world, or of the Partzuf, which include the ten Sefirot of direct light and the ten Sefirot of reflected light, in the manner clarified above in the Ohr Pnimi, that wherever reflected light ascends from below upward, those ten Sefirot are called by the name head, or Keter — except that the Rav discerns, within this head, two discernments of Keter: the first he names Atik, or the last "I", which includes the four phases in potential. And the second he names AA, or the first "I" (see in the Ohr Pnimi, Part 3, Chapter 7, Item 90), which includes the four phases in actuality. And the distinction between these two Keters has already been clarified above in the Ohr Pnimi mentioned; and here, in the Inner Observation, they will be clarified at length in their reasons and grounds.
And the Keter that includes all the worlds, called Adam Kadmon, is a matter distinct and different from all three discernments of Keter mentioned above: for the Keter of direct light is discerned as Ein Sof, blessed be He, before the restriction, as above. And the two Keters called Atik and AA are discerned according to their own merit, in that the screen operates within them from below upward, so that this reflected light cannot raise with it any of the coarseness that is in the screen, as above, and there is here no reckoning at all with the measure of stature of these ten Sefirot, as clarified, for even in Yetzira and Assiya these two Keters, Atik and AA, are discerned, as in the words of the Rav (Part 3, Chapter 6, Item 7 and Chapter 7, Item 5). Indeed, the world of Adam Kadmon, which is called Keter, is so only by reason of measure of stature alone, which depends on and is measured by the coarseness of the screen, for from the screen of phase four, the reflected light is found ascending and clothing up to Keter of direct light, whereas the reflected light of the screen of phase three is too short to clothe Keter, and reaches only up to Hochma (as written at length in the Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 65, Sub Header, "And from what has been clarified").
And since the screen of phase four operates only in the first world, called AK, therefore only in that world is the stature of the ten Sefirot found reaching up to Keter, and nowhere else; and for this reason all the degrees in that world are discerned at the level of Keter, even the degrees of the Guf and the degrees below the navel down to the conclusion, all are discerned at the stature of Keter, for the reason clarified.
Indeed, together with the above, one must know that these three kinds of Keter mentioned above also exist within AK itself, even though it is entirely Keter from its beginning to its end: for necessarily, the Keter of direct light within it is the discernment of Ein Sof before the restriction, as above. And likewise the two discernments of Keter called "head," whose reflected light goes from below upward, as above, apply here too, so that in this head the two Keters, Atik and AA, are always discerned, as above — except that they are called the particular Keter of AK itself, since it too has a head and a Guf, and the head is its particular Keter. Also within the head itself there is a Keter of direct light, which is the resting of the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, before the restriction, which is the particular Keter of the head itself.
And this is what the Rav writes: "the Keter that is in AK is four roots from the four discernments of the ten Sefirot within it, namely: souls, bodies, garments, and palaces, and this is by way of the particular." The meaning is, here he speaks of the discernment of the head called Keter, because the screen operates within it from below upward, as above, so that then the reflected light clothing it carries up no coarseness at all, and for this reason it is discerned only as roots of vessels, namely four roots for the four discernments of the vessels HB TM that will later be revealed in the Guf of AK, called: soul, body, garment and palace. And because they are only roots, they are therefore called by the name Keter, for every root is called Keter; whereas the four phases drawn after this from above downward are complete vessels in actuality, and these are called the Guf of Adam Kadmon (as written in its reason and ground in the Inner Observation, Part 2, Item 22, Sub Header, "And behold it has been clarified"), and therefore the Rav calls this head of AK by the name "Keter by way of the particular," meaning particular Keter, which is four roots for the four phases from above downward within it. And this is what the Rav writes: "but by way of the general, this is what is said now, that the generality of the discernments of souls in AK is called the root of the souls, etc. And likewise the generality of the discernments of bodies of AK is called the root of bodies, etc., and likewise the generality of the discernment of garments of AK is called the root of the garments, etc., and the generality of the discernments of palaces of AK is called the root of the 'palaces,'" end quote. For here he speaks of the discernment of Keter reckoned by measure of stature, by which discernment all the discernments existing in AK, from its beginning to its end, are discerned as Keter, as above — see there. And therefore the four phases within it that are below the head, namely those called complete vessels, whose reflected light descends from the screen downward, as above, are also discerned by the name Keter. And although, with respect to AK itself in its particularity, they are not called Keter, for only the head within it alone is called Keter, but they are called soul, body, garment and palace, which are the four Sefirot HB TM — nevertheless, with respect to the discernment of measure of stature, they too are called Keters for all the worlds, for the reason above, that the stature of Keter is found only in the world of AK. And therefore the Rav says that its Hochma, called soul, although found below the head of AK, is nevertheless discerned as the Keter for all the Hochmas found in the worlds; and its Bina, called body, is the Keter for all the Binas found in all the worlds. And its ZA, called garment, is the Keter for all the ZA found in the worlds. And its Malchut, called palace, is the Keter for all the Malchuyot found in all the worlds. For the reason is the same for all of them, namely, because the screen of phase four operates in them alone, and in no other world, as clarified.

items.html: The general Hochma, of Atzilut, is the root of the souls of the souls for all the worlds: Here too the Rav speaks only of the discernment of measure of stature, in the manner we explained regarding the four discernments HB TM of AK. And it has already been clarified above (Ohr Pnimi, Chapter 3, Item 2, Sub Header, "Indeed") that the four phases of Atzilut come from the reflected light ascending from the screen of phase three, wherefore the stature of the ten Sefirot of Atzilut begins only from Hochma, called soul. And therefore also in the world of Atzilut, all the discernments within it, from its beginning to its end, are reckoned at the discernment of Hochma and soul. And this is what the Rav writes, that the generality of the discernments of souls of Atzilut, namely Hochma, are the discernments of souls of souls for all the worlds, that is, at the discernment of Hochma, with respect to the Sefirot of Hochma of all the worlds. And likewise the bodies of Atzilut are called souls of bodies of all the worlds, and likewise the garments of Atzilut, and likewise the palaces of Atzilut, for the reason that they all emerged by clothing in the reflected light of phase three, which clothes up to the stature of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:9:4
items.html: And so with Beria, Yetzira and Assiya: This too is by reason of measure of stature, for all the ten Sefirot of Beria have only up to the stature of Bina, namely from the reflected light of the screen of phase two, as above (Ohr Pnimi, Chapter 3, Item 4), and therefore all the degrees within it are reckoned at the discernment called bodies, and even the Malchut of Beria is the discernment of Bina, with respect to the Malchuyot of all the worlds, that is, for the reason clarified. And likewise you will understand that all the discernments of the world of Yetzira are reckoned as garments, meaning as ZA, of all the worlds, because they come from the reflected light of phase one, whose stature is up to ZA, called garment. And likewise in the world of Assiya, all its discernments are palaces, meaning Malchut alone, without measure of stature. And likewise you will understand the whole continuation of the words of the Rav, and there is no need to elaborate further. (And here, in the Inner Observation, we shall expand on these matters.)
